why: All three limbs survive the challenge; the finding stands, with two scope corrections. (1) DOC — `curl -sL https://code.claude.com/docs/en/changelog.md` line 21 carries the quoted sentence VERBATIM: "Added `mcp_server_errors` to the headless stream-json init event, listing `--mcp-config` entries skipped by config validation; terminal runs print a startup warning". The WHOLE line is exactly that one bullet (bullet 4 under `<Update label="2.1.219" description="July 24, 2026">`, lines 17-40); the semicolon clause is part of the quote, and nothing later on the line or in the block reverses it. `changelog` is row 65 of `scripts/claude-doc-pages.tsv`, so it is a valid Claude contract page under the AGENTS.md citation rule. (2) CODE — `apps/cli/src/index.ts:457` sets `const streamJson = args.outputFormat === 'stream-json'`; inside the `client.on('session:event', ...)` subscription the only stream-json write is `if (streamJson) { process.stdout.write(JSON.stringify(ev) + '\n') }` — a raw passthrough of the server's `session:event` payload with no framing object. The cited line 468 is the blank line immediately above; the write is :469-471, an off-by-one in the citation, not a substantive error. `grep -ran -e 'mcp_server_errors' packages apps` → 0 hits (verified with `-a` for the NUL-byte trap). (3) CONSEQUENCE, verified separately from the identifier — the `AgentEvent` union in `packages/core/src/types/message.ts:967-1014` has no `init`, `system` or `mcp_server_errors` member at all (members are `status`, `info`, `text_delta`, `text_complete`, `pi_turn_anchor`, … `error`, `typed_error`, `usage_update`, `steer_undelivered`), so no layer upstream can supply the frame. Nothing is written to stdout before the first server event on either caller path. The only MCP failures our stream can carry are RUNTIME connection errors (`mcp_auth_required` / `mcp_unreachable`, `packages/core/src/types/message.ts:679-680`, raised in `packages/shared/src/agent/diagnostics.ts:363,374`) delivered mid-turn as `typed_error` — a different event at a different time from a startup config-validation report. Sibling-subsystem check: plugin-supplied MCP servers DO get validation diagnostics that reach a headless consumer, but through a separate command (`apps/cli/src/plugin.ts:252` groups them as 'MCP servers'; `:179-183, :314, :447` print/emit `diagnostics`), never through the `run`/`send` stream — so a CI consumer of `--output-format stream-json` still sees nothing. Not an owner decision: none of the nine dated entries in `docs/superpowers/specs/2026-07-29-inert-worklist.md` §3 (SEATBELT_TESTING_WILDCARD, availableModels/enforceAvailableModels, autoMode.classifyAllShell, ManagedDeliveryStateV1.drops, plugins/hooks-runtime.ts, SdkMcpServerConfig.required, SessionMirrorStore.delete, MirrorSessionKey.subpath/listSubkeys, listSessionSummaries/listSessions) touches headless output framing or MCP startup reporting. Not a de-brand or dropped-subscription difference: `nessy-general-agent run --output-format stream-json` is a shipped, documented format (`docs/cli.md:165`). TWO CORRECTIONS THAT NARROW IT. (a) Our CLI has NO `--mcp-config` flag — the complete flag list at `apps/cli/src/index.ts:80-157` is `--url --token --workspace --timeout --json --tls-ca --send-timeout --source --mode --output-format --json-schema --no-cleanup --disable-spinner/--no-spinner --verbose --safe-mode --server-entry --workspace-dir --provider --model --api-key --base-url --help --version --validate-server`, and `grep -ran 'mcp-config|strict-mcp|mcpConfig'` over `apps/cli/src`, `packages/server*/src` and `packages/shared/src` finds only unrelated plugin/mcpb identifiers. So even with an init frame the documented field would have no input on this surface; MCP servers here come from Sources and plugins, not a per-invocation config flag. The actionable gap is the missing init frame, not this field. (b) f133 is the same defect as f180 (`headless`, which already names `mcp_server_errors` among the missing init fields) and f125 (`best-practices`, the init-frame subset). Close them together — this is one defect counted three times, not three.
